correctness.rationale: With a universally accessing root, every failure of an implication at any world entails failure at the root; one global material counterexample therefore suffices. The explicit S subset, root-all relation rows and nonroot empty/singleton rows yield simultaneous induction on all subformulas. Closed formulas are independent of valuations, so original frame validity of finite X survives restriction. A finite guess of |I|+1 worlds, atoms and relevant relation matrices is polynomial and checkable; Boolean 3-SAT admits a polynomial many-one reduction to the dual-rail rooted encoding because root reflexivity forbids contradictory literal pairs. Replayed 1150 finite random witness compressions, an explicit four-world witness separation, and 360 small 3-CNF instances with the actual standalone checker; no infinite claim relies on these finite experiments.

value.rationale: A uniform exact witness-star normalization is a structural strengthening of the qualitative finite frame property on the newly introduced propositional FMT semantics: arbitrary nested formulas retain all subformula truth at every selected world, while every nonroot implication row is empty or shares one distinguished target. The linear world bound provides concrete polynomial root-satisfiability certificates and explains an NP-complete natural semantic decision problem for every fixed finite closed negative extension. The problem is motivated by Kurahashi–Noguchi’s finite-frame theorem and its explicit saturated-tableau rather than arbitrary small-instance arithmetic; the result does not claim unsupported optimality or consequences for other frame classes.
